raw:
I kept 13 of the 20 colleague hypotheses and replaced 7 weak ones. I didn't run any experiments or check any benchmark data, so this is judged from how the search space behaves.

**Kept:**
- **Capacity saturation:** edits on conv-rich parents should matter less (colleague items 4, 5, 8, 18, 20).
- **Missing capacity:** edits should matter more when a parent route is removed or is parameter-free (colleague items 1, 3, 9, 10, 17).
- **Borderline but kept:** items 2, 6 and 11. They are the weakest of the kept set, since their direction is more ambiguous.

**Dropped, because the direction was ambiguous or the mechanism was weak:**
- Edge 4 conv3x3 given edge 0 skip.
- Edge 2 conv3x3 given edge 1 skip.
- Edge 2 skip given edge 5 avg-pool.
- Edge 4 avg-pool given edge 1 skip.
- Edge 1 avg-pool given edge 3 conv1x1.
- Edge 0 skip given edge 4 conv3x3.
- Edge 3 skip given edge 5 conv3x3.

**Added:**
- **Dead-edge effects:** when edge 0 is `none`, node 1 is unreachable, so edits to edges 2 and 4 should do almost nothing.
- **Sole route:** when edge 1 or edge 2 is `none`, node 2 has only one remaining input route, so conv edits there should matter more.
- **Saturation:** edge 3 or edge 1 conv3x3 given a conv parent elsewhere should add less.
